events.text:
Türkiye unveiled Arı Kovanı (Beehive) at the Ateş Serbest-2026 exercise — a retractable-roof sentry shelter that rapidly deploys kamikaze FPV drones from a protected, fixed position. 
The monoblock booth features a mechanical opening roof and a rotary launch mechanism carrying 30 Gözükara FPV/loitering munitions on a 10-shelf conveyor system.
Shelves can be quickly refilled by the operator as they empty. 
The concept allows rapid vertical deployment of low-cost precision-strike drones for base defense or perimeter security without exposing operators — essentially an automated drone dispenser disguised as a guard booth.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
Ukrainian drone strikes on three Yandex data centers (Oct 8–11) have crippled Russia’s biggest tech company, with services still unstable six days later. 
Facilities in Sasovo and Vladimir were fully knocked offline, while Kaluga was partially hit — together taking down 80+ cloud services at peak and disrupting everyday apps millions of Russians depend on. 
Yandex Pay, Maps, Taxi, Navigator, and the Alice AI assistant remain glitchy or unavailable across multiple regions as of today. 
Yandex Cloud is in emergency mode with compute, databases, Kubernetes, and AI services degraded or offline.
The company waived fees through October and told customers to use backup options. 
Yandex says user money and data are safe but acknowledges prolonged access issues. 
The Vladimir facility alone was a 50 MW site designed for ~2,880 server racks. 
Physical repairs could take weeks to months depending on damage to servers, power, and cooling systems.

Over 40 laptop farms across Texas were dismantled by the FBI last month, with nearly 200 computer devices seized. The network helped North Koreans obtain remote IT jobs at U.S. companies using stolen American identities, funding Pyongyang's nuclear and ballistic missile programs.
Indictments were unsealed in Ohio against two U.S. nationals and 10 China-based North Koreans. Prosecutors say the scheme hit 70 companies for more than $3 million between 2019 and 2025.

🇷🇺🧊 Ukraine’s Starlink connection goes haywire amid latest Russian assault
Besides not being warned in advance by NATO ‘partners’ on Russia’s overnight missile strikes in Kiev, Ukrainian forces on the ground have reportedly faced “disrupted frontline operations” after[ new technical restrictions ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76157)were put in place on the use of Elon Musk’s satellite internet service.
Starlink terminals used to operate drones flying 160 km/h+ suffered “signal failures,” disrupting multiple missions Wednesday morning, Ukrainian officials and military personnel told FT.
💬 “Logistics at the frontline and middle strikes are badly limited,” a senior Ukrainian official said. There was “no warning,” with the restrictions just becoming apparent “in the middle of the night,” they said.
[Defense Ministry aide Serhii Beskrestnov said ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75939)it was obvious “this action is not coincidental and is related to the current political situation.”
👉 Musk has not made any formal announcement on the restrictions, but did recently accuse Zelensky of going “too far” by ignoring Trump’s energy ceasefire demands, and saying it’s “time for Ukraine to find a new leader.”
Trump insisted Tuesday that the US continues to do [intel sharing with Ukraine.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76143)
➡️ Musk previously restricted Ukraine’s Starlink access by geofencing coverage to limit Ukrainian strikes deep inside Russia. The US only once briefly paused intel sharing with Ukraine – in March 2025, after an explosive televised Trump-Zelensky exchange at the White House during which Trump accused his counterpart of “gambling with World War Three.”
The immediate chaos at the front once US intel and technological support are put on pause appears to confirm what Russian officials have been saying for almost five years – that this is a NATO proxy war that would end immediately if the West pulled its support for Kiev.
